name: Kaus Media
description: A star 107 parsecs away, 66 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 89931: radius 66.322 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1393.05 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.061) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 89931: effective temperature 4333 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.076)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 89931: distance 106.61 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.019), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 107 parsecs away, 66 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 1,393 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,333 K, so 66.322 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 89931: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Delta Sagittarii
quotes.card: Delta Sagittarii, formally named Kaus Media, is a star in the southern zodiac constellation of Sagittarius.
quotes.introduction: The apparent visual magnitude of this star is +2.70, making it easily visible to the naked eye.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 4049506483413484672 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
